title: Bands chain together: fragments far apart are merged into one band at a single position, so smears and band clusters come out as single sharp bands
description:
mergeItems (lane.ts:85-96) compares each fragment only with the previous one in the sorted list (`gap < resolution`). A run of fragments each closer than `resolution` to its neighbour becomes one band, however far apart its first and last fragments are. GelBand has only a mass-weighted mean `position` and `size`, with no top/bottom extent. The comment's promise of 'one wide band, like a smear' therefore cannot be drawn by the UI, which gets one point-like band. This breaks the spec ('fragments closer than the resolution threshold merge into one band') and gives a wrong gel picture for realistic inputs.

E. coli U00096.3 / EcoRI (646 fragments; same count, largest 42,844 bp and smallest 14 bp as Biopython 1.88) on 1 % TAE gives 5 bands:
- bands[0] holds 528 fragments from 42,844 to 1,180 bp, whose own positions span 0.195 to 0.587 of the gel.
- It is reported at one position, 0.260, with size 14,895 bp and intensity 1.
- Every other band gets intensity 0.0000 to 0.011, so it is effectively invisible.

MboI (19,124 fragments) gives 5 bands; one holds 19,107 fragments spanning 0.469 to 0.899, drawn at 0.746.

This also happens at BAC scale. A 150 kb window of U00096.3 (1,000,000 to 1,150,000) cut with EcoRI gives 28 fragments in Biopython. On 0.8 % TAE:
- the six fragments from 9,971 to 14,083 bp (ends 0.029 apart, about 3x the resolution) become one band at 0.286 reported as 12,124 bp;
- 592/574/528 become another band (spread 0.014).

Suggested fix: either cap each band's width at the resolution (complete linkage or fixed windows), or add the extent (min and max fragment position) to GelBand so a smear can be drawn. Also consider not letting a smear's total mass set the lane's brightness scale.
expected: Only fragments closer than the resolution end up in the same band: every band's member fragments lie within about 0.01 of each other. Alternatively, a merged band reports its extent so the UI can draw the documented 'wide band / smear'. A genome or BAC digest should not come out as a few sharp bands at mass-weighted mean sizes.
actual:
BAC test: the band 14083/13222/12268/11559/10627/9971 has spread 0.0295 (expected < 0.01).
Dense-series test: 35 fragments in one band at 0.533 with spread 0.140.
E. coli EcoRI test: 528 fragments in one band at 0.260 (14,895 bp, intensity 1) with spread 0.392; the remaining 4 bands have intensities of 0.011 or less.

title: Bioneer massNg values are 2 to 2.5 times the ng in the vendor's recommended load, against the spec's definition of massNg
description:
The spec defines `LadderBand.massNg` as 'ng in the vendor's recommended load'. For three Bioneer ladders the stored values are the vendor table's ng per 4 µl or 5 µl. Bioneer manual PM-338, which is the ladders' own `source`, has a Specifications table:
- D-1020: 150 ng/µl, recommended 2 µl per 5 mm lane
- D-1030: 100 ng/µl, recommended 2 µl
- D-1035: 80 ng/µl, recommended 4 µl
- D-1040: 100 ng/µl, recommended 2 µl

Its band tables are labelled '(ng/4 µl)' for D-1040, D-1035 and D-1020, and '(ng/5 µl)' for D-1030. I extracted these strings from the PDF; the implementer's own `notes` also say 'recommended load 2 µl per 5 mm lane'.

The resulting errors at the recommended load:
- bioneer-1kb: masses sum to 400 ng, against 200 ng recommended (2x).
- bioneer-100bp: 500 ng against 200 ng (2.5x).
- bioneer-25-100bp: 600 ng against 300 ng (2x).
- bioneer-100bp-plus: 320 ng = 4 µl, which is correct.

ladderLane passes these values through as `GelBand.massNg`. Example: the D-1040 1,000 bp band reports 60 ng, but holds 30 ng when 2 µl is loaded as recommended.

Estimating DNA amount by comparing a sample band with a ladder band is a main use of mass ladders, and Bioneer ladders are common in Korean labs. A UI that shows massNg as the spec defines it would over-estimate DNA by 2 to 2.5 times.

The recommended load exists only as free text in `notes`, not as a data field. A UI therefore cannot rescale with bandMassAtLoad without parsing prose. NEB N3232 (0.5 µg table = 0.5 µg recommended) and N3200 (1.0 µg table, 0.5 to 1 µg recommended) are consistent; I checked them through r.jina.ai.
expected: massNg is the ng per band at the vendor's recommended load: totals of 200 ng (D-1040), 200 ng (D-1030) and 300 ng (D-1020), and 30 ng for the D-1040 1,000 bp band. Alternatively, Ladder has a structured recommended-load field so the UI can rescale with bandMassAtLoad.
actual: Totals are 400, 500 and 600 ng (expected 200, 200 and 300). ladderLane reports 60 ng for the D-1040 1,000 bp band. The recommended load appears only as prose in `notes`.

title: A merged band can't be traced back to its fragments: labels and sizes are in different orders and lengths, and there is no fragment index
description:
GelBand has `labels` (top to bottom; unlabelled fragments are left out) and `sizes` (largest first), and nothing that links one fragment's label, size, form or input index. When fragments merge, the UI cannot say which fragment a label belongs to. A tooltip such as 'EcoRI–BamHI: 1,010 bp' or selecting the fragment on the map when the band is clicked is impossible.

- Two different inputs, `[{1010,'b'},{1000}]` and `[{1010},{1000,'b'}]`, give exactly the same output (`labels ['b']`, `sizes [1010, 1000]`).
- With circular forms the two orders differ. Supercoiled 3,000 bp runs like 2,100 bp linear DNA and merges with a linear 2,150 bp fragment, giving `labels ['insert', 'uncut plasmid (SC)']` but `sizes [3000, 2150]`. A UI that pairs them by index labels the insert as 3,000 bp.

This matters for partial digests, where uncut supercoiled plasmid co-migrates with linear fragments. Suggested fix: include per-fragment records (input index, size, label, form, position) in each GelBand, in one consistent order.
expected: Each band lets the UI recover, for every member fragment, its label, size, form and input index, in one consistent order.
actual: Both inputs return [{size: 1005.02, position: 0.61796, intensity: 1, count: 2, labels: ['b'], sizes: [1010, 1000]}]. The circular-form case returns labels ['insert', 'uncut plasmid (SC)'] with sizes [3000, 2150], so pairing by index gives 'insert=3000'.

title: Inputs that pass validation can still produce NaN (simulateLane intensity, ladder components, bandMassAtLoad)
description:
The lens requires that outputs never contain NaN. Three paths produce NaN or invalid numbers without any error:
- simulateLane accepts any finite size and molarAmount, but `mass = size * amount` (lane.ts:160) can overflow to Infinity. The lane then has intensity Infinity/Infinity = NaN (JSON shows null), which breaks the documented 'brightest band = 1'.
- ladderLane checks band `size` and `massNg` but copies `components` unchecked (lane.ts:192). A custom ladder with components [NaN, -3] gives GelBand.sizes [NaN, -3] and count 2, breaking 'sizes ... largest first' and positivity.
- bandMassAtLoad (ladders.ts:360-364) checks only the `loadNg` argument. A NaN `ladder.loadNg` or `band.massNg`, for example from a user-defined ladder, returns NaN.

The overflow needs extreme values. The unchecked components and masses are plausible for custom ladders that users enter.
expected: Either a RangeError for invalid components or masses and for overflowing amounts, or finite outputs: intensity in (0, 1], sizes finite and positive.
actual: simulateLane([{size: 2000, molarAmount: 1e306}]) gives intensity NaN. ladderLane gives sizes [NaN, -3]. bandMassAtLoad returns NaN, as does a band with massNg NaN.

title: Built-in ladders are frozen at runtime but typed as editable, so ordinary sort/reverse code compiles and then throws a TypeError
description: LADDERS is deep-frozen (ladders.ts:336-348), but `Ladder.bands` is typed `LadderBand[]` and the Ladder and LadderBand fields are not readonly. `getLadder()` returns `Ladder`. Normal UI code such as `ladder.bands.reverse()` or `.sort(...)` to list bands smallest first passes `tsc --noEmit` with no errors (checked) and then throws 'TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property '0' of object '[object Array]'' at runtime, which would crash a React render. The `readonly Ladder[]` on the outer array doesn't help because the nested fields are still editable. Suggested fix: type LADDERS and getLadder as deeply readonly (readonly bands, Readonly<LadderBand>), or return copies.
expected: Either the types forbid editing (the compiler rejects l.bands.reverse()), or the call works at runtime.
actual: tsc passes; at runtime: TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property '0' of object '[object Array]'.

title: Validation errors don't name the bad fragment or ladder band
description: simulateLane and ladderLane stop at the first invalid entry with a message that gives only the bad value. They don't include the fragment's index or label, or the ladder's id and band index (lane.ts:153, 155, 187, 190; migration.ts:254 for forms). A UI that builds a lane from a list of user-entered or imported fragments can't point at the bad row. The lens asks for enough context in errors for a React UI to explain them.
expected: The error names the offending entry: the fragment index or label (e.g. 'fragment 2 (custom-3): size must be ...'), or the ladder id and band index.
actual: 'fragment size must be a finite number > 0 bp, got NaN' and 'ladder band size must be > 0 bp, got 0', with no index, label or ladder id.

title: Single-linkage merging chains fragments far apart into one point-like band (dense digests reported as a single band)
description:
mergeItems() (lane.ts lines 85-125) compares each fragment only with its immediate neighbour (`previous = item.position`, line 96; `gap < resolution`, line 94). Any run of fragments whose consecutive gaps are below the resolution therefore becomes ONE GelBand, however far apart its ends are. That band is reported at a single mass-weighted position, with a mass-weighted `size`, summed intensity and no extent, so a renderer can only draw it as a single sharp band. This breaks the spec rule that only 'fragments closer than the resolution threshold merge into one band'. The doc comment's claim that the chain 'becomes one wide band, like a smear' is not borne out, because GelBand carries no width. The same root cause affects ladderLane.

Reproduced at default settings (1% TAE, resolution 0.01) unless stated:
(a) Three fragments 0.009 apart (outer pair 0.018 apart) give 1 band.
(b) pBR322/MspI, the NEB N3032 marker fragments (identical to Biopython 1.88 on fixture J01749), gives one band at 0.840 holding 15 fragments from 242 to 67 bp, spread over 0.0615 of the gel (6x the resolution).
(c) A synthetic 1-40 kb smear of 300 fragments gives 1 band at 0.243, size '20,620 bp', count 300, intensity 1, although its fragments run from 0.196 to 0.619.
(d) E. coli MG1655 (fixture U00096.3) cut with EcoRI, 646 fragments from Biopython: the first band sits at 0.260 and holds 528 fragments of 1,180-42,844 bp, whose positions span 0.392 of the gel (intensity 1; all other bands at 0.01 or less). At 0.7% the whole genomic digest is 2 bands. A real gel shows a smear.
(e) A BAC-sized insert (U00096.3 bp 1,000,001-1,150,000) cut with EcoRI gives six fragments of 9,971-14,083 bp reported as one '12,124 bp' band (spread 0.023). The model itself separates the 10 and 8 kb ladder bands, which are only 0.019 apart.
(f) λ/AluI: one band holds 127 fragments of 6-603 bp (spread 0.19).
(g) Ladder lanes: NEB 100 bp at 3% TBE, inside NEB's recommended 1.2-3% range, merges the 1000, 900 and 800 bp bands.

This is not among the report's known limitations; it is presented as intended behaviour (lane.ts line 82).
expected: Per the spec, only fragments closer than `resolution` share a band. No band should contain fragments farther apart than the resolution, or else the band must carry its extent so a smear can be drawn. A genomic digest should come out as many bands or a smear over roughly 0.2-0.6 of the gel. Six BAC fragments of 10-14 kb should be at least partly resolved at 1% agarose.
actual: A chain of any length collapses into one GelBand at the mass-weighted mean position. pBR322/MspI at 1% gives one band spanning 0.0615 (6x the resolution). A 1-40 kb smear gives 1 band at 0.243 ('20,620 bp', intensity 1). E. coli/EcoRI gives a band at 0.260 holding 528 fragments that span 0.392 of the gel. A BAC/EcoRI digest gives one '12,124 bp' band holding 9,971-14,083 bp. NEB 100 bp at 3% TBE merges 1000+900+800.

title: Model places larger fragments too far from the well in high-% TBE gels; a fresh 3% TBE vendor photo fails the module's own < 2% RMS criterion
description: oracle.test.ts line 195 requires RMS < 0.02 for vendor photos that show the wells and state their conditions, but only two such photos were used, both 1% TAE. I tested a fresh photo of the same kind that the implementer did not use: Thermo GeneRuler Low Range (MAN0013037 p.2, embedded image xref 47), 3% agarose, 1X TBE, 8 cm gel, 5 V/cm, 1 h, wells visible (well peak 6.6 px below the image edge, the same as SM1331's 16.15). I measured it with the implementer's documented lane-profile method; that method reproduced their SM1331 rows exactly. With the same one-scale 'absolute' fit, RMS is 0.0352. The residuals run monotonically from +0.079 at 700 bp down to −0.031 at 25 bp: the model puts the 700 bp band at 0.240 of the gel where it is observed at 0.161. The 3% TBE curve's top asymptote is 0.142, so fragments above roughly 1 kb cannot be placed where the observed trend puts them. The bias has the same sign on every TBE photo at 1.7% or more: the implementer's own 1.7% TBE (+0.060 at 3 kb) and 2% TBE (+0.086 at 2 kb), and fresh NEB N3236 50 bp ladder on 3% TBE (+0.075 at 1,350 bp, affine) and Thermo GeneRuler 50 bp on 2.5% TBE (+0.065 at 1 kb, affine). The claimed 0.019 pooled accuracy does not extend to high-% TBE. All the other fresh photos I tested (NEB N3234 1.8% TBE, N3014 λ-BstEII 1%) are within the implementer's tolerance.
expected: RMS < 0.02, the module's own criterion for vendor photos with visible wells and stated conditions, with the largest band within a few % of the gel.
actual: RMS 0.0352. The 700 bp band is predicted at 0.240 against 0.161 observed (+0.079, about 6 mm on the 8 cm gel). The residual is monotone and same-signed across all TBE photos at 1.7% or more.

title: Lane merging chains neighbours (single linkage): fragments far apart are reported as one thin band
description:
`mergeItems` (lane.ts lines 90-97) compares each fragment only with the previous one. A run of fragments that are each less than `resolution` apart therefore collapses into ONE band, placed at the mass-weighted mean, however far apart the first and last fragments are.

`GelBand` has no width, so the UI draws one thin, bright band where the real gel shows resolved bands or a smear. This contradicts:
- the spec: "fragments closer than the resolution threshold merge";
- the TSDoc of `LaneOptions.resolution`: "fragments whose positions differ by less merge".

Cases reproduced with new inputs (Biopython 1.88 digests of fixture pBR322_J01749.gb, plus the E. coli fixture):
- pBR322/MspI on 2% TAE: 201, 190 and 180 bp become one band (0.018 apart).
- pBR322/HaeIII on 3% TBE: 587, 540 and 502 bp become one band (0.018 apart).
- E. coli U00096.3 / MspI (24,311 fragments, count confirmed with Biopython): the lane has only 4 bands. One band holds 24,307 fragments of 4–2,606 bp spread over 0.469 of the gel.

The failing regression tests in src/gel/lane.test.ts ("review: a band never joins fragments farther apart than the resolution") already cover this defect.
expected: No band contains fragments whose positions differ by more than `resolution` (0.01). A genomic digest gives many bands, or a smear the viewer can draw (its GEL_SMEAR_THRESHOLD is 160 bands).
actual:
- pBR322/MspI, 2% TAE: '201/190/180: expected 0.01801618271550931 to be less than or equal to 0.01'.
- pBR322/HaeIII, 3% TBE: '587/540/502: expected 0.01831580608462907 to be less than or equal to 0.01'.
- E. coli: '4 bands; widest: 24307 fragments 4-2606 bp: expected 0.46882750682189905 to be less than or equal to 0.01'.

title: GelBand.labels and GelBand.sizes are not index-aligned, so a merged band cannot be traced back to its fragments
expected: ['uncut 3000 SC -> 3000', 'insert 2150 -> 2150']: one entry per fragment, in the same order as `sizes` (or explicit fragment indices on the band).
actual: ['insert 2150 -> 3000', 'uncut 3000 SC -> 2150']: labels are in position order, sizes are sorted largest first.

title: simulateLane returns intensity NaN for inputs that pass validation (mass overflow or underflow)
description:
The mass is computed as `size * molarAmount` without normalisation (lane.ts line 160), then `b.intensity /= maxMass` (line 134). Validation accepts both of these inputs:
- A finite product that overflows to Infinity gives Infinity/Infinity = NaN.
- A positive amount whose product underflows to 0 gives 0/0 = NaN.

The band then reaches the UI with `intensity` NaN; the viewer silently drops bands whose intensity is not greater than 0.

The overflow case is already in lane.test.ts ("review: inputs that pass validation never produce NaN"). The underflow path is new.
expected: Intensity 1 for the single (brightest) band, or a RangeError naming the fragment. Never NaN.
actual: 'expected NaN to be 1'. Both calls return a band with intensity NaN (verified separately for the underflow case: `{ size: 0.5, position: 0.8999…, intensity: NaN, … }`).

title: ladderLane does not validate LadderBand.components: NaN or negative sizes leak into GelBand.sizes, and a long list crashes with a stack overflow
description:
`ladderLane` (lane.ts line 192) copies `b.components` into `sizes` without any checks. For a custom ladder, this has two effects:
- `components: [NaN, -3]` produces `GelBand.sizes = [NaN, -3]`, and `size` (500) lies outside its own `sizes`.
- A band with 200,000 components makes `mergeItems` call `sizes.push(...it.sizes)` (line 115), which throws "RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded" instead of a validation error. JavaScriptCore, the engine of the Tauri webview on macOS and Linux, caps spread arguments at about 65,536, so the limit there is lower.

The NaN half is already in lane.test.ts ("custom-ladder components are not copied unvalidated"). The crash is new.
expected: A RangeError naming the bad component, or only finite positive sizes; no stack overflow for a long list.
actual:
- First test: 'expected false to be true' (sizes = [NaN, -3]).
- Second test: "expected 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' not to match /call stack/". It also crashes at 500,000 and 1,000,000 components.

title: Validation errors do not say which fragment or ladder band is invalid
description:
The `simulateLane` and `ladderLane` errors (lane.ts lines 153, 155, 187, 190, and `formSizeFactor`) give only the bad value. They omit:
- the fragment's index or label;
- the ladder id and band index.

The UI cannot point the user at the offending row: one bad fragment among hundreds from a digest or an imported table produces "molar amount must be a finite number >= 0, got -1".

The failing regression tests in lane.test.ts ("review: validation errors name the bad fragment or ladder band") already cover this defect.
expected: The message names the fragment (index and/or label) or the ladder (id and band index).
actual: "expected 'molar amount must be a finite number >= 0, got -1' to match /custom-3|index 2|#2|\[2\]/". For a ladder, the message is 'ladder band size must be > 0 bp, got 0'.

title: bandMassAtLoad returns NaN for a NaN reference load or NaN band mass
description:
`bandMassAtLoad` (ladders.ts line 362) tests `ladder.loadNg <= 0`, which is false for NaN, and never checks `band.massNg`. A custom ladder with `loadNg: NaN`, or a band with `massNg: NaN`, therefore yields NaN. The TSDoc promises either a number or undefined, and a RangeError only for a bad load.

The failing regression test in ladders.test.ts ("review: bandMassAtLoad never returns NaN") already covers this defect.
expected: undefined, or a RangeError naming the bad field.
actual: 'expected true to be false': `bandMassAtLoad` returns NaN.

title: Ladder types are mutable but LADDERS is deep-frozen: mutation type-checks then throws, and immutable custom ladders are rejected
description:
`Ladder.bands` is typed `LadderBand[]` and `LadderBand.components` `number[]` (ladders.ts lines 25 and 43), yet `LADDERS` is deep-frozen. This has two effects:
- **Runtime TypeError:** `getLadder(id)!.bands.sort(...)` or `.reverse()` type-check, then throw at runtime. The type checker even reports the `@ts-expect-error` as unused (TS2578).
- **Rejected custom ladders (new angle):** a lab ladder kept as immutable data (`as const`, or a deep-readonly store) cannot be passed to `ladderLane(ladder: Ladder)` without a cast (TS2345).

The runtime half is already in ladders.test.ts ("review: built-in ladders are typed read-only").
expected: `Ladder`/`LadderBand` use readonly arrays, so mutating a built-in ladder fails at compile time and `as const` ladders type-check.
actual:
tsc output:
- `gel-robustness-types.test.ts(14,21): error TS2345: Argument of type '{ readonly id: 'lab-ladder'; … readonly bands: readonly [{ readonly size: 3000; }, …]; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Ladder'.`
- `(19,3): error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.`

Vitest output: "TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property '0' of object '[object Array]'".

title: DYE_COMIGRATION_BP and RESOLVING_WINDOW_BP are only frozen at the top level: one stray write changes or breaks the whole model
description:
`Object.freeze` is applied to the outer arrays only (migration.ts lines 121-142). The `[percent, bpb, xc]` rows that every `migrate`, `simulateLane`, `ladderLane`, `sizeAtPosition` and `resolvingWindow` call interpolates from stay mutable at runtime. `LADDERS`, by contrast, is deep-frozen.

A write through a cast or from JS code (the row types are readonly only at compile time):
- silently shifts every later position (writing 380 into the 1% TAE row moves 1 kb from 0.6189 to 0.6233);
- or, with a larger value (3700), makes every later call at 1% TAE throw "migration model has no solution at 1% TAE" for the rest of the session.

The module-level calibration state is shared by all lanes, so the damage is module-wide.
expected: Rows are frozen like `LADDERS` (the write throws TypeError in strict mode), so the model cannot change after load.
actual:
- First test: 'expected false to be true' (rows not frozen).
- Second test: 'expected { after: 0.6233076587102581, … } to deeply equal { after: 0.618923085233781, … }'.
- Third test: "expected 'migration model has no solution at 1%…' to be '(no throw)'". Before the test restored the row in a `finally` block, this also broke every later test in the same file.

title: The NEB 500/517 bp doublet is reported as 500 bp by one ladder and 508.5 bp by the other, contradicting the GelBand TSDoc
description:
`GelBand.size` and `GelBand.position` are documented (lane.ts lines 45-48) as mass-weighted means of the band's fragments. The same physical doublet comes back differently from the two NEB ladders:
- **N3232 (`neb-1kb`):** two rows (517 and 500 bp, 21 ng each). `ladderLane` merges them into size 508.5, at the mean position.
- **N3200 (`neb-1kb-plus`):** one row with `components: [517, 500]`. The band has sizes [517, 500] but size 500 and position `migrate(500)`.
- **Promega 250/253:** same pattern.
- **At resolution 0:** the doublet is one band in N3200 and two in N3232.

Visible effect in the UI: packages/viewer/src/gel/layout.ts labels ladder bands with `formatGelSize(band.size, 'ladder')`. At the default 1% TAE, NEB 1 kb is labelled "509 bp", a size that appears in no vendor documentation, while NEB 1 kb Plus is labelled "500 bp" for the same band.
expected: One convention for both ladders: either the vendor's nominal size (and the TSDoc says so), or the documented mass-weighted mean (508.5) with the mean position.
actual:
- First test: 'expected { size: 500, …(1) } to deeply equal { size: 508.5, …(1) }'.
- Second test: 'neb-1kb-plus 500/517: expected 500 to be close to 508.5, received difference is 8.5'.

title: TBE calibration distorts band positions and spacing at 1.7-2.5 % agarose; simulateLane merges 1000 bp and 910 bp, which the vendor gel resolves
description:
At 1.0-1.5 % TBE the model's TBE curve fits the vendor photos well (NEB and Bioneer 1 % TBE: affine RMS 0.003-0.009). From 1.7 % TBE upward the curve has the wrong shape. On every TBE photo at 1.7 % or more, the model's own TAE curve for the same agarose % fits the TBE photo 2.5-5 times better than its TBE curve:
- thermo-sm0321 at 1.7 % TBE: TBE curve RMS 0.0336, TAE curve 0.0134.
- bioneer-d1020 at 2 % TBE: TBE 0.0345, TAE 0.0162.
- A FRESH photo not in vendor_gels.json (Thermo GeneRuler 50 bp DNA Ladder, MAN0013016 Rev. C.00 p.2: 2.5 % agarose, 1X TBE, 5 V/cm, 1 h, 8 cm gel; band rows measured from the embedded image): TBE 0.0447, TAE 0.0088.

The residual is S-shaped: the TBE curve compresses the top of the lane and stretches the bottom. At 2.5 % TBE the 1000/900 bp spacing is 0.57x the photo and the 100/50 bp spacing is 1.34x.

Practical effect at the default resolution: 1000 bp and 910 bp are 0.0093 apart on the 2.5 % TBE curve, so simulateLane merges them into one band at 957 bp. The vendor photo implies about 0.016 of separation. The model's 2.5 % TAE curve gives 0.0181, consistent with the photo, and resolves the pair.

The existing 3 % TBE regression test covers a different symptom: at 3 % the TBE shape fits acceptably (affine RMS 0.021) but the absolute positions are off. A fix aimed only at that test can leave 1.7-2.5 % TBE wrong. 2 % TBE (0.5X TBE) is a standard condition for PCR products and the default buffer of Bioneer's ladders.
expected: For the stated condition (2.5 % TBE), the model should reproduce the vendor photo about as well as its claimed pooled accuracy (RMS about 0.02). Its buffer-specific curve should fit TBE photos at least as well as the TAE curve does. 1000 bp and 910 bp should be two bands at the default resolution, as on the vendor's 2.5 % TBE gel.
actual:
- Affine RMS is 0.0447 at 2.5 % TBE.
- The TAE curve fits all three TBE photos at 1.7 % or more better: 0.0134 vs 0.0336, 0.0162 vs 0.0345, 0.0088 vs 0.0447.
- The 1000/900 bp spacing is 0.57x the photo.
- simulateLane([{size:1000},{size:910}], {agarosePercent: 2.5, buffer: 'TBE'}) returns a single merged band at 957 bp.

title: Enzynomics DM003 note gives the wrong total of the printed band masses (720 ng; they add up to 740 ng)
description: The enzynomics-1kb-plus (DM003) ladder note says 'The per-band amounts printed by the vendor add up to 720 ng per 5 µl (nominal 750 ng).' The vendor's figure (Amount ng/5 µl: 10000 40, 8000 40, 6000 40, 5000 80, 4000 40, 3000 40, 2000 80, 1500 40, 1000 80, 800 30, 650 30, 500 60, 400 30, 300 30, 200 40, 100 40) adds up to 740 ng. The ladder's own massNg values (correctly transcribed) also add up to 740. The note is user-facing metadata described as 'caveats copied from the vendor documentation', and the implementer's report repeats the wrong figure ('480, 720 and 540 ng'). The DM002 (480) and DM001 (540) notes are correct.
expected: The DM003 note states the total of the vendor's printed per-band amounts: 740 ng per 5 µl (nominal 750 ng).
actual: The note says 720 ng, while the band masses in the same ladder object add up to 740 ng.
